chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning the demolition of a wall in which three men had participated. It fell upon one of them and he died, so he held the other two liable for his blood money, because each one of them is responsible for his companion.

key_terms.دِيَتَهُ: his blood money; the financial compensation due for his death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if three people jointly demolish a wall and it kills one of them?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning shared liability in a joint act that resulted in death. It establishes that when several people jointly undertake the demolition of a wall and one of them is killed by its collapse, the remaining participants bear responsibility for his diyah due to their mutual involvement.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5361 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who narrated from Abu Basir, who narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"The Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled regarding the demolition of a wall in which three people participated. When it collapsed on one of them and caused his death, he held the remaining two responsible for his blood money because each one of them is accountable for his companion."
